questions.q: If a student evenly mixes Yellow and Blue paints, what secondary colour will be produced?
questions.explain: Yellow and Blue are primary colours. When mixed together, they produce the secondary colour Green.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Mixing the primary colours Red and Blue will result in which colour?
questions.explain: Red and Blue mixed together produce Purple (also known as Violet).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a Tertiary Colour?
questions.explain: Yellow is a primary colour, Orange is a secondary colour, and Blue is a primary colour. Yellow-Green is a tertiary colour, formed by mixing Yellow and Green.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: In colour theory, adding black to a pure hue to make it darker creates a:
questions.explain: A shade is created when you add black to a colour. Adding white creates a tint, and adding grey creates a tone.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: What typically happens if you mix all three primary paint colours (Red, Yellow, Blue) together?
options: You get a muddy dark brown or near-black colour.
The colours separate and will not mix.
You get a bright neon colour.
questions.explain: Because paint subtracts light, mixing all three primary pigments absorbs most of the light, resulting in a dark, muddy, neutral color like dark brown or black.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
